title: Distributed GAN with Swift Learning Mechanism for Multiparty Tabular Data Synthesis
summary: Synthesises tabular data held by several parties who share a schema but cannot share records, for cases like fraud detection across banks. The generated tables are evaluated by machine-learning efficacy, the protocol SDMetrics established, against generators in the CTGAN line.
evidence: tabular data generated from parties were trained under a machine learning efficacy evaluation; CTGAN is cited as the tabular GAN lineage rather than run directly

title: Assessing Privacy-Utility Trade-offs in Generative Models for Tabular Data
summary: Measures what differential privacy costs in utility by running generators with and without formal guarantees over the same tabular data. CTGAN and TVAE are the unprotected pair, trained on the real data and compared against PATE-CTGAN and DPGAN.
evidence: we demonstrate two GMs without explicit privacy protection, such as CTGAN and TVAE; CTGAN and TVAE are trained on real tabular data

title: Enhancing IoT Network Security through Intelligent Data Augmentation
summary: Augments IoT network traffic to give intrusion detectors enough attack examples to learn from. ACTGAN is the generator, a conditional tabular architecture in the CTGAN line rather than the library itself.
evidence: section 'The ACTGAN Model': the ACTGAN model employs a structured approach to generating conditional tabular data

title: A GAN-Augmented Ensemble Learning Framework for Early Heart Disease Risk Prediction
summary: Predicts early heart disease risk from a clinical dataset whose positive and negative cases are badly unbalanced. CTGAN is trained on the processed records and sampled to produce synthetic patient profiles, with the conditional component steering which class is generated.
evidence: section 'C. Balancing Class Using CTGAN'; a large enough number of synthetic profiles of heart patients were then generated by the trained CTGAN

title: SynthLogAI: Generative AI for Synthetic Linux Kernel Log Generation
summary: Compares six generators on the unusual task of producing Linux kernel logs, evaluated against real LTTng traces for fidelity, distinguishability and scaling. CTGAN is the tabular model in the comparison and comes out the most balanced, holding categorical and numeric distributions from 1K to 100K traces where the language models degrade.
evidence: for each trace size we generate a synthetic dataset using each generator: CTGAN, LSTM, and GPT-2; CTGAN achieves the most balanced performance and scales well from 1K to 100K

title: A Stochastic Diffusion Framework for Tabular Data Synthesis
summary: Proposes a diffusion framework for tabular synthesis and scores it against earlier generator families on correlation preservation. CTGAN is one of the GAN-based baselines measured.
evidence: GAN-based generators (CTGAN, TableGAN) generally achieve lower CPS on datasets with strong correlation structure
